title: Desk Guidance: Inactivation, Reactivation and Closure Figures for Employer UI Tax Accounts
content:
An account within the Employer Unemployment Insurance Tax Accounts is inactivated after 4 consecutive quarters with no wages reported, can be reactivated with its experience within 8 quarters after inactivation, and closes only with a final report filed and a zero balance due. These figures are the same in every financing class.

| Financing class | Zero-wage quarters before inactivation | Reactivation window (quarters after inactivation) | Final report required to close | Balance due must be zero to close |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Contributory — New Employer Standard Rate | 4 | 8 | Yes | Yes |
| Contributory — New Employer Construction Rate | 4 | 8 | Yes | Yes |
| Contributory — Experience-Rated Positive Reserve | 4 | 8 | Yes | Yes |
| Contributory — Experience-Rated Deficit Reserve | 4 | 8 | Yes | Yes |
| Contributory — Delinquent Reporting Assigned Rate | 4 | 8 | Yes | Yes |
| Reimbursing — Nonprofit Organization | 4 | 8 | Yes | Yes |
| Reimbursing — Governmental Entity | 4 | 8 | Yes | Yes |

## Points of judgement the figures settle

- **Zero-wage quarters before inactivation (4).** The account is inactivated once the consecutive quarters with no wages reported reach 4. A run of 3 such quarters has not reached the figure; a run of 4 has.
- **Reactivation window (8 quarters).** Wages resuming within 8 quarters after inactivation reactivate the same account with its experience.
- **Final report required (Yes).** A final report, marked as the last quarter of wages, is required to close the account.
- **Balance must be zero (Yes).** The balance due must be zero before the account closes; a balance of USD 0.01 still owed does not meet the figure.
